motive: He needed the Pulse wall at full brightness for the 10 PM demonstration and had no spare module.
method: After reading the high-severity DO NOT POWER warning at 20:49 and finding no spare, he restored power to Module 04 at a real 21:32 through the rear loading door. Arjun later entered by the main door and was shocked diagnosing the powered cabinet.
explanation: Reckless, knowing conduct: he knew the unit was unsafe and powered it anyway. The records do not support an intentional attack.

timeline.event: Kavya powers Module 04 off (controller reads 20:43, already the reference time)
Kavya files MR-184: connector too hot, DO NOT POWER
Priya reminds Rohit of the full-brightness demo; he answers "Give me ten minutes" at 21:30
Controller shows ON at 21:29 (3 minutes slow) and the rear-door camera shows motion at displayed 21:36 (4 minutes fast)
Arjun enters the main workshop door

causal_chain: Module 04 was reported unsafe and Rohit read the warning.
There was no spare and the demo was due at 10 PM.
After correcting the clocks the controller ON and the rear-door motion are the same real minute.
The rear door generates no RFID event, so no workshop entry exists for the person who restored power.

resolution.motive: Pressure to deliver the full-brightness demo at 10 PM with no spare module.
resolution.method: He knowingly powered a quarantined module that had been marked DO NOT POWER.
chain: He read the Module 04 warning at 20:49.
He found no spare and told Priya "Give me ten minutes".
The corrected controller time and the corrected rear-door camera time agree at 21:32.
The rear door produces no RFID record; his task list says restore full-brightness demo.
